e: A court rules that Argentina must return an 18th century painting stolen by Nazis from a Dutch Jewish art collector and missing for eighty years prior to being photographed in 2025 hanging in the house of the daughter of a senior SS officer, who had fled to Argentina after World War II, to the rightful owner's heir.
A federal judge is removed from office by the Jury of Impeachment over antisemitic social media posts for the first time in over a century.
The United States imposes a 10% tariff on Argentina, citing the presence of alleged forced labor in the supply chain.
Argentina finishes second at the 2026 FIFA World Cup after losing to Spain 1–0 at the final.
The body of 14-year old Agostina Vega is found sexually assaulted, dismembered and hanged in Córdoba, triggering nationwide protests.
The EU–Mercosur Partnership Agreement comes into effect.
Authorities at Ezeiza International Airport seize more than 700 living and dead marine animals trafficked from Kenya.
President Milei orders the expulsion of the entire presidential press corps from the Casa Rosada, citing unauthorized filming inside the office.

Argentina expels Iranian chargé d'affaires Mohsen Soltani Tehrani after Iranian officials issue statements that Argentina describes as false and offensive. The move follows Argentina's designation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as a terrorist organization.
A 15-year-old student fatally shoots another student and injures eight others at a school in San Cristóbal, Santa Fe, before being taken into custody.
Foreign minister Pablo Quirno announces the country's formal withdrawal from the World Health Organization.
Iran war: Argentina expresses support for the United States and Israel in the war against Iran.
The Argentine Senate ratifies the EU–Mercosur Partnership Agreement.
A general strike is held in protest against a labor reform bill proposed by the Milei government.
Argentina and the United States sign a trade agreement reducing tariffs on most goods.

The government declares the Muslim Brotherhood and its associate chapters in Egypt, Jordan, and Lebanon as terrorist organizations. The organizations include the Muslim Brotherhood in Egypt, the Islamic Group, and the Islamic Action Front.
